note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Acute left-sided headache began this morning (woke at ~05:30), persistent at time of consult; patient has prior history of less severe headaches.
- Clinician assessed likely tension-type headache versus migraine; advised trial of ibuprofen, sleep/hydration measures, stress reduction, counseling referral, and follow-up in one week.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Acute unilateral headache (today)
- Presentation: Woke with severe left-sided head pain at ~05:30 this morning; headache still present during consult.
- Timeline/progression: Onset this morning, woke patient from sleep; dizziness on waking which has since subsided.
- Associated symptoms: Mild photophobia (eyes sore with bright light), no nausea, no fever, no neck stiffness.
- Medications/response: Took paracetamol this morning — not effective.
- Examination: No in-person examination performed.
- Differential diagnosis: Tension-type headache versus migraine (clinician stated both possibilities).
- Plan related to this issue: Start ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented); may continue paracetamol if desired; advised rest, sleep 7–8 hours/night, hydrate 1.5–2 L/day (excluding coffee/tea); return if worse or new symptoms; follow-up appointment in one week; consider blood tests or further evaluation if no improvement.

Issue 2: History of anxiety on long-term SSRI
- History: Anxiety for approximately two years; currently taking sertraline.
- Current status: Some work-related anxiety occasionally; denies suicidal ideation.
- Social/medication: Sertraline is being taken (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Relevance: Clinician identified stress/anxiety as possible contributor to headaches.
- Plan related to this issue: Encourage counseling/self-referral (link to local service to be provided); consider time off work to reduce stress.

Issue 3: Work-related stress, sleep disruption, and possible contributing lifestyle factors
- History/timeline: Increased work stress and many late nights for approximately two months.
- Social/behavioral: Runs ~3 times/week; diet “OK” (not unhealthy); lives with partner; non-smoker; has a cat.
- Pertinent negatives: No alcohol or smoking reported (alcohol intake not quantified in transcript).
- Plan related to this issue: Advise taking time off work (suggested one week self-certify), counseling referral, optimize sleep and hydration as above; clinician provided patient education and link to red flag symptoms.

Medications:
- Sertraline — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Paracetamol — taken this morning (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Ibuprofen — recommended as first-line for suspected migraine/tension-type headache (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies reported ("Not that I'm aware of").

Past Medical History:
- Anxiety disorder (≈2 years).
- Recurrent headaches historically, described as less severe and usually frontal rather than unilateral.

Social History:
- Lives with partner.
- Non-smoker.
- Has a cat.
- Exercises: running approximately three times per week.
- Work: current significant stress and late nights for ~2 months.
- Diet: described as "OK" / not unhealthy.
- Alcohol: not discussed/quantified.

Preventative History:
- Cervical screening test: not documented.
- Mammogram: not applicable/not documented.
- Prostate blood test: not documented.
- Faecal occult blood test: not documented.
- Bone mineral density: not documented.
- Vaccination status: not documented.
- Recent optometry review/skin check/other preventive visits: not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: not documented.
- Examination findings: No physical or neurological examination performed during this remote consult.

Plan:
- Start ibuprofen for headache (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Continue/allow paracetamol if desired (already taken this morning without benefit).
- Advise minimum 7–8 hours sleep per night.
- Advise hydration 1.5–2.0 L/day (excluding coffee/tea).
- Recommend taking time off work (suggested one week self-certify) to reduce stress.
- Provide link for local counseling service for self-referral.
- Documented red flag/danger-sign information link to be placed in notes for patient review.
- Follow-up arranged in one week with same clinician or another GP.
- If no improvement at follow-up, consider blood tests or further investigation.
- Patient advised to recontact earlier if symptoms worsen or new concerning signs develop.
